issues.legal_issue: A landowner’s conditional consent to acquisition does not prevent a challenge to the acquisition when the consent was an unaccepted offer withdrawn before acceptance.
material_facts: During the compensation inquiry, the landowner said he was willing to have his land acquired if he received lump-sum compensation.
The acquiring officer did not accept the offer or make an award before the landowner withdrew it.
The landowner later challenged the acquisition proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The landowner was entitled to withdraw the unaccepted offer, and his conditional consent did not bar his challenge to the acquisition.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Contract Act, a statement of willingness to accept acquisition on a stated condition amounts to an offer; until acceptance there is no contract, and the offeror may withdraw the offer. No earlier cases are relied on for this ruling.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: A landowner challenged proceedings to acquire the land.
predicates.conditional_consent_offer: The landowner offered to accept acquisition subject to a stated condition.
predicates.offer_unaccepted_when_withdrawn: The acquiring authority had not accepted the offer before the landowner withdrew it.

issues.definition: When a landowner challenges an acquisition after withdrawing an unaccepted conditional offer, the withdrawn offer does not bar the challenge.

issues.legal_issue: Failure to publish the substance of an acquisition notification in the locality within the required period invalidates the acquisition.
material_facts: A notification proposing to acquire land was published in the Government Gazette.
The substance of the notification was published in the locality more than forty days later.
The applicable amended requirement made publication within forty days mandatory.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition was bad in law because the substance of the notification was not published in the locality within forty days of its Gazette publication; any possession taken had to be returned.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as amended by the Andhra Pradesh (Amendment) Act, 1983, made the forty-day period for publication of the substance of the notification in the locality mandatory. Non-compliance renders the acquisition bad in law. No earlier cases are identified by the Court as the basis for this ruling.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: An authority undertook proceedings to acquire land.
predicates.required_local_publication_deadline_exce: The acquiring authority published the substance of the acquisition notice in the locality after the required period had expired.

issues.definition: An acquisition proceeding in which the acquiring authority publishes the notice’s substance locally after the required period results in an invalid acquisition.
